card.statement: A nonzero object $B$ is said to be stable if every non-trivial sub-object $A\subset B$ satisfies $A\prec B$. Equivalently, $B$ is stable if every non-trivial quotient-object $B\to C\to 0$ satisfies $B\prec C$. A nonzero object $B$ is said to be semistable if every non-trivial sub-object $A\subset B$ satisfies $A\preceq B$. Equivalently, $B$ is semistable if every non-trivial quotient-object $B\to C\to 0$ satisfies $B\preceq C$.
card.label: Definition 2

paper.title: On Moduli Spaces for Abelian Categories
paper.abstract: We show that if A is an abelian category satisfying certain mild conditions, then one can introduce the concept of a moduli space of (semi)stable objects which has the structure of a projective algebraic variety. This idea is applied to several important abelian categories in representation theory, like highest weight categories.
